collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 35 or older and another adult)

collection.description: Two villagers who talk over every harvest are asked about all of life: try to answer, or stick to this year.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the end of every harvest, (subject) and (friend) sit on the storehouse step and do the same thing: they talk about the year. What went well, what went badly, what they'd do differently. They've done it for so many years now that it's become a sort of ritual. This year, (friend) suddenly asks, "What about the whole thing? Not this year. All of it?"

choices.label: Say Let's Stick to This Year

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) is quiet for a long time. "Mostly good," (subject.he/she) says at last. "Some terrible bits. More good bits than I expected. A lot of bits I can't decide about." (friend) nods. "Same." They sit and watch the sun go down. It's the shortest, most honest answer either of them has ever given to anything.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Too big," says (subject). "One year at a time." (friend) laughs. "Fair." They go back to talking about the beans, which did badly, and the yams, which did wonderfully, and the pig, which ate the squash. It's comforting, somehow, to talk about the squash. The whole of life can wait for next harvest.
